artiest/bireli-lagrene-en-sylvain-luc.text:
Biréli Lagrène and Sylvain Luc are two French jazz guitarists who also play together. Lagrène was born in 1966 in Soufflenheim, in Alsace, into a Romani family. His father and grandfather were guitarists, and he grew up in the Gypsy guitar tradition. He began playing at four or five and at seven was already improvising jazz in the style of Django Reinhardt, whom his father admired. In 1980, still in his early teens, he recorded his first album, Routes to Django: Live at the Krokodil.

In the years that followed he toured with guitarists such as Al Di Meola, Paco de Lucía and John McLaughlin and played with Benny Carter, Benny Goodman and Stéphane Grappelli. He performed with Jaco Pastorius, Stanley Clarke and the Gil Evans Orchestra. His style stretches across swing, jazz fusion and post-bop. He won several Django d'Or awards and, in 2001, a Victoire de la Musique for the album Front Page.

Two guitars in a duo show how much a stringed instrument can say without a band around it: one plays melody, the other chords and rhythm, and they take turns. Lagrène brings the Reinhardt tradition of the French Romani guitarists into a modern jazz language, and that makes this duo a fine link between the swing of the 1930s and the jazz of today.
artiest/bireli-lagrene-en-sylvain-luc.listen: Listen to Made in France. Notice how the two guitars pick up and answer each other's ideas, and which of the two is playing the melody at any given moment.

artiest/bismillah-khan.text: Bismillah Khan turned the shehnai, an oboe-like instrument heard mainly at weddings and temples, into an instrument for the classical concert platform. He was born in Dumraon, grew up in Varanasi and practised on the banks of the Ganges. On 15 August 1947 he played at the Red Fort in Delhi as the Indian flag was raised. In 2001 he received the Bharat Ratna, India's highest honour.
artiest/bismillah-khan.listen: Listen to Raga Todi and hear how the shehnai glides from note to note, almost like a singing voice.

artiest/bix-beiderbecke.text: Bix Beiderbecke grew up in Davenport, Iowa, and taught himself to play the cornet by copying records of Nick LaRocca's Original Dixieland Jass Band. In 1924 he made his first recordings with The Wolverines. He heard Louis Armstrong play on the riverboats of the Mississippi. His own tone was clear and round, and his solos were melodic and well constructed, unlike Armstrong's hot style. With the saxophonist Frankie Trumbauer he recorded Singin' the Blues in 1927, one of the most influential solos of the 1920s. On piano he wrote In a Mist, with harmonies that recall Debussy. He then worked in Paul Whiteman's big orchestra. He died in 1931, aged 28.
artiest/bix-beiderbecke.listen: Listen to the calm, round cornet tone in Singin' the Blues: few notes, well chosen.

artiest/biz-markie.text:
Biz Markie's real name was Marcel Theo Hall. He was born in Harlem in 1964 and grew up on Long Island, near New York. He took his stage name from one of the first hip hop acts he heard, with the rapper Busy Bee. He began in nightclubs in New York and performed at universities on the East Coast. He belonged to the Juice Crew around the producer Marley Marl and the label Cold Chillin', and helped the rapper Roxanne Shanté with beatboxing.

His debut album Goin' Off appeared in 1988, with Make the Music with Your Mouth, Biz and Vapors. The Biz Never Sleeps (1989) contained his biggest hit, Just a Friend, with a chorus based on a soul song by Freddie Scott. Biz Markie was known for his humour; he was called the clown of hip hop. His raps were playful, and he sang his choruses without caring about hitting the right note.

In 1991 his third album, I Need a Haircut, changed hip hop history. The singer Gilbert O'Sullivan sued him because the track Alone Again used a piece of his Alone Again (Naturally) without permission. The judge ruled in O'Sullivan's favour and the album was pulled from the shops. From then on, permission had to be asked for, and paid for, with every sample. Biz Markie responded in 1993 with the wink of All Samples Cleared! He died in 2021.
artiest/biz-markie.listen: Listen to Just a Friend. Notice the simple piano accompaniment and the chorus, which Biz Markie sings himself, deliberately a little flat and with a great sense of humour.

artiest/bjork.text:
Björk Guðmundsdóttir was born in 1965 in Reykjavík and grew up with her mother in a communal household. At six she went to music school, where she learned classical piano and flute. When her teachers sent a recording of her singing to the radio, she was offered a record contract. Her first album, Björk (1977), appeared when she was eleven. As a teenager she played in punk bands, jazz-rock groups and the gothic band Kukl. From 1986 she became internationally known as the singer of The Sugarcubes.

After the end of that band in 1992 she began a solo career. On Debut (1993), Post (1995) and Homogenic (1997) she mixed electronic dance music, pop and avant-garde, with hits such as Big Time Sensuality, Army of Me, Hyperballad and It's Oh So Quiet. She went on searching: Vespertine (2001) sounded intimate and crackling, Medúlla (2004) consisted almost entirely of voices, and Biophilia (2011) came with an app. Later she worked with the Venezuelan producer Arca, and Fossora (2022) she produced entirely on her own. As an actress she won a prize at Cannes for the film Dancer in the Dark.

Björk has a striking voice with a range of three octaves, which can whisper, scream and soar. She sets the course of her music herself and makes many of the beats and arrangements herself. In this way she became a model for women who not only sing but also take charge of the sound of their records as producers.
artiest/bjork.listen: Listen to Army of Me. Notice the heavy, growling synthesizer bass and the hard beat, and how Björk sings against them with her powerful, almost menacing voice.

artiest/bjorn-ulvaeus.text:
Björn Ulvaeus was born in 1945 in Gothenburg and grew up in Västervik. As a boy he listened to blues musicians such as Muddy Waters, Howlin' Wolf and John Lee Hooker. In the 1960s he became known as a member of the Hootenanny Singers, a Swedish group that sang folk music and schlager and had many fans in Scandinavia. In 1966 he met Benny Andersson, the keyboard player of The Hep Stars, while on the road. They discovered a shared love of songwriting and became a regular duo.

Björn and Benny worked as producers at Stig Anderson's label Polar and wrote hits for others. In 1969 Björn met the singer Agnetha Fältskog, whom he married in 1971. Benny by then had a relationship with Anni-Frid Lyngstad. ABBA grew out of the collaboration of the two couples. Björn played guitar, sometimes sang lead himself, as in Does Your Mother Know and Summer Night City, and wrote most of the lyrics. Together with Benny he wrote and produced all the ABBA albums, with a sound finished down to the smallest detail.

After ABBA the duo continued working together. With Tim Rice they made the musical Chess (1984), then the Swedish musical Kristina från Duvemåla and Mamma Mia!, built on the ABBA hits, which also spawned two films. Björn Ulvaeus is an example of a songwriter who turned Swedish schlager into a worldwide successful pop factory.
artiest/bjorn-ulvaeus.listen: Listen to Does Your Mother Know by ABBA, on which Björn Ulvaeus sings lead. Notice the rocking guitars and the fast rhythm, and the backing vocals of Agnetha and Frida answering his singing.

artiest/bl-f.text:
BLØF, pronounced 'bluff', is a pop band from Vlissingen, formed in 1992. The band sings in Dutch and emphatically holds on to its roots in Zeeland. The permanent core consists of the singer and guitarist Paskal Jakobsen, the bassist Peter Slager, who writes the lyrics, the keyboard player and guitarist Bas Kennis and the drummer Norman Bonink.

The breakthrough came in 1998 with Liefs uit Londen, from the album Helder. Hits followed such as Harder dan ik hebben kan, Dansen aan zee and Mooie dag. In 2001 the drummer Chris Götte was killed in a road accident, and Bonink took his place. The album Omarm (2003) was a great success, and in 2004 BLØF reached number 1 in the Top 40 with Holiday in Spain, together with the American band Counting Crows. For Umoja (2006) the band recorded songs with musicians from thirteen countries.

Zoutelande (2017) is a Dutch-language version of Frankfurt Oder by the German singer Bosse. Slager moved the song to the Zeeland village of Zoutelande. The hit version is a duet with the Flemish singer Geike Arnaert, formerly the voice of Hooverphonic. In 2018 the song spent ten weeks at number 1 in the Top 40 and six weeks at number 1 in Flanders. That same year it reached number 31 in the Top 2000. Since 2006 BLØF has organised the festival Concert at SEA on the Brouwersdam. In this way the band stayed connected, through its songs and its festival, to the region it comes from.
artiest/bl-f.listen: Zoutelande is a duet: listen to how Paskal Jakobsen and Geike Arnaert alternate and find each other in the chorus. The melody comes from a German song about Frankfurt an der Oder; only the lyrics were moved by Peter Slager to the Zeeland coast.

artiest/black-flag.text:
Black Flag is an American punk band founded in 1976 in Hermosa Beach, California, by the guitarist Greg Ginn and the singer Keith Morris, under the name Panic. Morris was originally going to drum, but Ginn found his energy and charisma so great that he became the frontman. The band had difficulty finding a permanent bassist and often rehearsed without one, which contributed to Ginn's idiosyncratic guitar sound. Most of the material appeared on Ginn's own label SST Records.

They are regarded as one of the first hardcore punk bands and as a pioneer of post-hardcore. In 1981 Henry Rollins joined as singer, the year of the album Damaged with Rise Above. In 1984 came My War, Family Man and Slip It In, in 1985 In My Head and Loose Nut. In 1986 the group broke up. Reunions followed in 2003 and 2013, with the album What The… in 2013, and a legal dispute between Ginn and the group FLAG.

The sound combines the raw simplicity of the Ramones with atonal guitar solos. The lyrics deal with resistance to authority, social isolation, poverty and paranoia. Later, influences from heavy metal, free jazz and contemporary classical music were added, and the band played longer, slower songs in a scene of fast three-chord numbers. Black Flag is considered a key figure of American punk, especially on the West Coast.
artiest/black-flag.listen: Listen to Rise Above. Notice the fast, raw guitar and Rollins's screaming vocals, and how short and urgent the song is.

artiest/black-francis.text:
Black Francis is the stage name of Charles Michael Kittridge Thompson IV, born on 6 April 1965 in Boston, Massachusetts. He is a singer, songwriter and guitarist and the lead singer of the alternative rock band Pixies. His father ran a bar and his parents introduced him early to the folk rock of the 1960s. His first guitar was a classical Yamaha belonging to his mother. When he was twelve, his mother and stepfather joined an evangelical church, and you can see that in the biblical references in many Pixies songs. He studied anthropology at the University of Massachusetts Amherst, and lived there with Joey Santiago, the later guitarist of Pixies.

After Pixies split up in 1993 he began a solo career under the name Frank Black, with fifteen albums and his own band The Catholics. Pixies got back together in 2004, and in 2013 he declared his solo career over. Later albums under the name Black Francis are Bluefinger in 2007 and NonStopErotik in 2010.

His voice sounded shrieking and wailing with Pixies, and more restrained and melodic in his solo work. His enigmatic lyrics deal with surrealism, UFOs, biblical violence, science fiction and surf culture. Notable are the unusual time signatures, the switching between soft and loud and, with The Catholics, recording live to two tracks. In this way he gave alternative rock a style of its own, on which many bands later built.
artiest/black-francis.listen: Listen to a Pixies song in which his singing alternates between soft and screaming, and notice the switching between the two. Notice how the band around him shifts from quiet to loud.

artiest/black-sabbath.text:
Black Sabbath formed in 1968 in Aston, a working-class district of Birmingham. The guitarist Tony Iommi and the drummer Bill Ward wanted to start a heavy blues rock band and found the bassist Geezer Butler and the singer Ozzy Osbourne, who had put up an advertisement in a music shop. The group was first called the Polka Tulk Blues Band and then Earth. Opposite their rehearsal room an Italian horror film was showing, Black Sabbath. Butler thought it strange that people spent so much money on being frightened, and the band wrote a song of the same name. In August 1969 they adopted that name for the band too.

The song Black Sabbath used the tritone, an interval also known as the devil's interval. That menacing sound did not fit at all with the cheerful flower power of the late 1960s. The debut Black Sabbath, recorded live in two days, and Paranoid both appeared in 1970, followed by Master of Reality (1971). With low-tuned guitars, crushingly heavy riffs, slow tempos and lyrics full of horror and occult themes, the band wanted to make the musical equivalent of a horror film.

In 1979 Osbourne was fired and Ronnie James Dio took over, with whom Heaven and Hell (1980) came about. Many changes followed, until the original line-up reunited. Together with Led Zeppelin and Deep Purple, Black Sabbath laid the foundations of hard rock and above all heavy metal. In 2025 the band gave a final concert in Birmingham.
artiest/black-sabbath.listen: Listen to the song Black Sabbath from the album of the same name. Notice the opening with rain and a church bell, and then the slow, heavy three-note guitar riff that sounds so ominous.

artiest/blind-willie-johnson.text:
Blind Willie Johnson was an American gospel blues singer and guitarist, born on 25 January 1897 in Pendleton, Texas, and died on 18 September 1945. His father, a sharecropper, gave him his first instrument at the age of five, a guitar made from a cigar box. He was not born blind. According to most biographers he lost his sight at seven when his stepmother splashed him with lye water, a story told by his widow Angeline Johnson. He wanted to become a Baptist minister and played religious songs on street corners, with a tin cup attached to his guitar to collect money.

He made his best-known recordings between 1927 and 1930, thirty songs in five sessions. These include Dark Was the Night, Cold Was the Ground, a hymn without words in which his slide guitar plays the leading part. He also recorded Jesus Make Up My Dying Bed, It's Nobody's Fault but Mine and John the Revelator. His records sold well, but as a street musician and preacher he had little money. Little about his life was recorded, and historians such as Samuel Charters later worked out part of it.

In the 1960s there was renewed interest in him, through his inclusion in Harry Smith's Anthology of American Folk Music and through Reverend Gary Davis. Both are regarded as the most important players of holy blues, religious lyrics in blues style. Dark Was the Night, Cold Was the Ground was given a place on the golden records of the Voyager space probes that NASA launched in 1977. Johnson combined a heavy chest voice, slide guitar and inventions of his own, and influenced generations of musicians.
artiest/blind-willie-johnson.listen: Listen to Dark Was the Night, Cold Was the Ground and notice that you hear no words, only his guitar and a humming voice. Try to hear how the slide sings like a human voice.

artiest/blink-182.text:
Blink-182 is an American rock band that formed in August 1992 in Poway, a suburb of San Diego in California. The guitarist Tom DeLonge met the drummer Scott Raynor at a Battle of the Bands, and through acquaintances came into contact with the bassist Mark Hoppus. The group grew out of the skate punk scene of Southern California and stood out for its energetic performances and silly humour. The first albums, Cheshire Cat in 1995 and Dude Ranch in 1997, appeared on an independent label and brought success in San Diego and in Australia.

In 1998 Raynor was fired and Travis Barker joined on drums. The band then signed with MCA Records. The 1999 album Enema of the State, with All the Small Things, and Take Off Your Pants and Jacket from 2001 were their biggest successes. Dammit and What's My Age Again? also became hits and staples of MTV. Later came, among others, blink-182 in 2003, Neighborhoods in 2011, California in 2016 and One More Time in 2023. DeLonge left the group twice; in his absence Matt Skiba of Alkaline Trio played with them.

The sound is called pop punk: catchy pop melodies combined with fast punk rock and simple arrangements. The lyrics deal with relationships, teenage frustration and not wanting to grow up. In this way they gave pop punk a new step towards the mainstream in the late 1990s.
artiest/blink-182.listen: Listen to All the Small Things. Notice how short and simple the chords are and how the chorus in particular sticks in your head.

artiest/blondie.text:
Blondie is an American rock band founded in New York in 1974 by the singer Debbie Harry and the guitarist Chris Stein. Stein played with the Stillettoes, where Harry was one of the singers. In July 1974, together with the drummer Billy O'Connor and the bassist Fred Smith, they started a new band, which after a few names came to be called Blondie in October 1974. The group belonged to the CBGB scene of the mid-1970s and is regarded as a pioneer of new wave.

The debut album Blondie from 1976 remained an underground record, and Plastic Letters from 1977 brought the first successes in the United Kingdom and Australia. The breakthrough came in 1978 with Parallel Lines, followed by Eat to the Beat in 1979 and Autoamerican in 1980. They contain hits in various styles: Heart of Glass, One Way or Another, Dreaming, Call Me from the film American Gigolo, Atomic, The Tide Is High and Rapture. Rapture was the first number one on the Billboard chart with rapping. After the failure of The Hunter in 1982 the band broke up, partly because of tensions, money worries and Stein's serious illness. In 1997 it came back, and No Exit from 1999 brought it success again, with Maria as its sixth number one in the United Kingdom.

Blondie mixed punk, pop, disco, reggae and hip hop in short, infectious songs and showed that the styles of the New York street could come together in one band. In 2006 the group was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame.
artiest/blondie.listen: Listen to Heart of Glass from Parallel Lines (1978) and notice the rhythm, which is danceable and comes from disco. Hear how the vocals stay cool and even above that beat.

artiest/blur.text:
Blur formed in London in 1988. The singer and keyboard player Damon Albarn and the guitarist Graham Coxon had known each other since childhood; at Goldsmiths College they met the bassist Alex James, and the drummer Dave Rowntree completed the band. At first they were called Seymour, after a story by J.D. Salinger. Their record company Food did not think that was a good name, and so in 1990 it became Blur. Together with Oasis, Blur was the biggest band of Britpop.

The debut Leisure (1991) produced the hit There's No Other Way. On Modern Life Is Rubbish (1993) and Parklife (1994) the band sought out English everyday life, with characters and small stories, as The Kinks had done in the 1960s. The album Parklife entered at number 1 and stayed ninety weeks in the British album chart. At the Brit Awards of 1995 Blur won four prizes, including best band and best album. In August 1995 Country House won the 'Battle of Britpop': in the first week 274,000 copies were sold, against 216,000 of Roll With It by Oasis.

Afterwards the band distanced itself from the English sound. The album Blur (1997) contains Song 2, two minutes long, with a distorted bass and Albarn's shouted 'woo-hoo'. Some writers see it as a parody of grunge. On 13 (1999) and Think Tank (2003) Blur searched further; Coxon left during the recording of Think Tank. Albarn started the virtual band Gorillaz with the artist Jamie Hewlett. In 2009 Blur came back with concerts in Hyde Park, and in 2023 The Ballad of Darren appeared.
artiest/blur.listen: Parklife (1994): notice the division of roles. The actor Phil Daniels speaks the verses in a broad London accent, while Damon Albarn sings only the chorus. It sounds like music hall, the British variety theatre of around 1900.

artiest/bo-diddley.text:
Bo Diddley was born in 1928 in McComb, Mississippi, as Ellas Otha Bates. A cousin of his mother raised him, and he took her surname, McDaniel. When he was five the family moved to the South Side of Chicago. At church he learned trombone and violin, but he was drawn even more to the rousing, rhythmic music of a Pentecostal church in the neighbourhood. He took up the guitar, inspired by John Lee Hooker, and performed on street corners and at the Maxwell Street market.

In 1955 Chess Records released his first single, with I'm a Man and Bo Diddley. The latter became a number 1 hit on the R&B chart. At his shows Jerome Green sat next to him with the maracas, and the two liked to trade funny insults. Songs such as Who Do You Love? (1956) followed. That same year he was allowed to appear on the Ed Sullivan Show, but because he played a different song from the one agreed, he was never asked back.

Bo Diddley played striking rectangular guitars and used tremolo and reverb effects. His trademark was a simple, stuttering five-beat rhythm, with roots in African and Latin American music. That rhythm, the Bo Diddley beat, became a building block of rock, pop and later hip hop. He influenced Buddy Holly, The Rolling Stones, The Animals and The Clash, and so helped make the transition from blues to rock 'n' roll.
artiest/bo-diddley.listen: Listen to Bo Diddley from 1955. Notice the chopping five-beat rhythm on the guitar, the shaking maracas and the trembling, reverberating guitar sound. There is almost no chord change: the rhythm is everything.

artiest/boards-of-canada.text:
Boards of Canada is a Scottish duo of the brothers Mike Sandison and Marcus Eoin, who have made music together since 1986. They grew up in Cullen and later in Balerno near Edinburgh, and lived in Calgary in Canada from 1979 to 1980. As children they were already experimenting with tape recorders and layering sound fragments over compositions of their own. The name comes from the National Film Board of Canada, an institution whose documentaries and animated films they saw as children. Only in 2005 did they say in an interview that they are brothers.

In 1998 they signed with Warp Records and released the debut album Music Has the Right to Children, which includes Roygbiv, an album now considered a high point of electronic music. Geogaddi followed in 2002, darker in tone, and The Campfire Headphase in 2005 with more real instruments. In 2013 came Tomorrow's Harvest, inspired by film music, and in 2026 Inferno.

Their sound revolves around old synthesizer sounds, analogue equipment, samples and beats that resemble hip hop. It is influenced by the public broadcasting of the 1970s and is about nostalgia, childhood memories, science and the environment. The duo is regarded as a pioneer of intelligent dance music and of hauntology. They give almost no interviews and have not performed live since 2001.
artiest/boards-of-canada.listen: Listen to Roygbiv. Notice the warm, slightly distorted synthesizer sounds and how the slow beat underneath keeps going.

artiest/bob-dylan.text:
Bob Dylan was born in 1941 as Robert Allen Zimmerman in Duluth, Minnesota, and grew up in the mining town of Hibbing. In 1961 he moved to New York, where in the cafés of Greenwich Village he became part of the folk revival. He showed that a pop song could be about more than falling in love. In 2016 he received the Nobel Prize in Literature, 'for having created new poetic expressions within the great American song tradition'.

His debut album Bob Dylan (1962) consisted mainly of old folk songs, such as House of the Rising Sun in the arrangement of Dave Van Ronk. The Freewheelin' Bob Dylan (1963) contained songs of his own such as Blowin' in the Wind and A Hard Rain's a-Gonna Fall. He then chose electric guitars. Bringing It All Back Home (1965) was his first album with an electric band, and at the Newport Folk Festival of July 1965 his electric set was both cheered and booed. Like a Rolling Stone, over six minutes long, reached number two on the Billboard Hot 100 that year. In 1966 followed the double album Blonde on Blonde, recorded in Nashville.

Dylan's influence ran in two directions. The Byrds turned his Mr. Tambourine Man into an electric number 1 hit, and with that folk rock got a face. The Beatles met him in August 1964 in New York, and their lyrics became more personal afterwards. In the Netherlands, Boudewijn de Groot and Lennaert Nijgh sang protest songs in the same spirit, and Nijgh translated The Times They Are A-Changin'. In 1988 Bruce Springsteen played Dylan's Chimes of Freedom in East Berlin.
artiest/bob-dylan.listen: Like a Rolling Stone opens with a single hard crack on the snare drum. Then listen to the Hammond organ: Al Kooper was a guest at the recording and was not really supposed to play. Dylan had the organ turned up louder in the mix, and between the lines it plays an answer of its own to the vocals.

artiest/bob-geldof.text:
Bob Geldof was born in 1951 in Dún Laoghaire, near Dublin. His mother died when he was eight. At school he was bullied and beaten. He then worked in, among other places, a slaughterhouse, road construction and a canning factory, and later as a music journalist in Vancouver, Canada. In 1975 he returned to Ireland and became the singer of The Boomtown Rats, a rock band closely tied to punk and new wave.

The band had two number 1 hits in England that Geldof co-wrote: Rat Trap (1978) and I Don't Like Mondays (1979). He wrote the latter after a shooting at a primary school in San Diego. Geldof was known as a fierce and brash talker, who attacked politics and the Catholic Church on an Irish talk show. In 1982 he played the lead role in the film Pink Floyd: The Wall.

In 1984 he saw the television reports on the famine in Ethiopia. Together with Midge Ure he wrote Do They Know It's Christmas?, which they recorded as Band Aid with a group of British and Irish stars. A year later they organised the great benefit concert Live Aid, and in 2005 the Live 8 concerts followed. For his efforts he received an honorary title from the British Queen. Geldof showed how popular music could mobilise a worldwide audience for a good cause.
artiest/bob-geldof.listen: Listen to I Don't Like Mondays by The Boomtown Rats. Notice the piano that carries the song and how the song slowly builds to a big, almost theatrical chorus, while the lyrics are about a shocking event.

artiest/bob-marley.text:
Bob Marley was born in 1945 in Nine Mile, a village in Jamaica. His mother was Afro-Jamaican, his father a much older white Englishman whom he hardly knew. At twelve he moved with his mother to Trenchtown, a poor district of Kingston. There, with his friend Bunny Wailer, he listened to ska and to American R&B on the radio. With Bunny and Peter Tosh he formed a vocal group, which eventually became known as The Wailers. Their neighbour Joe Higgs taught them to sing together and taught Marley to play guitar.

In 1964 Simmer Down became a number 1 hit in Jamaica. In the late 1960s Marley converted to the Rastafari faith and grew dreadlocks. With the producer Lee Perry the group made some of its best work. After a contract with Island Records the band broke through internationally with Catch a Fire and Burnin' (both 1973). After Tosh and Bunny left, Marley continued with Natty Dread (1974), Rastaman Vibration (1976) and Exodus (1977). A live version of No Woman, No Cry became his first hit outside Jamaica, and Eric Clapton scored with his I Shot the Sheriff.

Reggae revolves around a heavy, melodic bass, a guitar that strikes briefly on the offbeat and a relaxed rhythm. Marley filled that music with spirituality, resistance and hope. He died in 1981 of cancer, only 36 years old. In this way he became a worldwide symbol of Jamaica and of reggae.
artiest/bob-marley.listen: Listen to Stir It Up by Bob Marley & The Wailers from 1973. Notice the difference between the heavy, melodic bass and the guitar that plays short and dry on the offbeat. Hear how calm Marley's singing remains above it.

artiest/bob-marley-en-the-wailers.text:
Bob Marley & The Wailers was a Jamaican band that began with ska and rocksteady and grew into the best-known reggae group in the world. The group formed in 1963 in Trench Town, a poor district of Kingston, with the singers Bob Marley, Peter Tosh and Bunny Wailer. In 1964 they had a number 1 hit in Jamaica with Simmer Down, recorded at Studio One with musicians from The Skatalites. The song called on the rude boys, the rebellious youths of the city, to stay calm. It helped Jamaican musicians to sing about their own lives instead of imitating foreign artists.

Around 1970 they worked with the producer Lee Scratch Perry, who experimented with reverb and echo in the studio. From his band came the bassist Aston Family Man Barrett and the drummer Carlton Barrett, who would form the rhythm of the Wailers. In 1972 they received an advance from Chris Blackwell of Island Records. On the album Catch a Fire (1973) the sound was adapted to the rock audience in England and America. Burnin' followed, with Get Up, Stand Up and I Shot the Sheriff. The typical reggae sound consists of a heavy, melodic bass, drums that put the emphasis on the second and fourth beats and a guitar that plays short chords on the offbeat.

In 1974 Tosh and Wailer left. Marley carried on with the female singers of the I-Threes and albums such as Natty Dread, Exodus and Uprising. His songs about resistance, faith and love made reggae known worldwide. After his death in 1981 the band came to an end.
artiest/bob-marley-en-the-wailers.listen: Listen to Stir It Up from 1973. Notice the difference between the bass, which plays heavy and melodic, and the guitar, which plays short chords between the beats, on the offbeat.

artiest/bob-moses.text:
Bob Moses is a Canadian electronic music duo based in Vancouver, which formed in New York. It consists of the singer Tom Howie and the producer Jimmy Vallance. Both went to the same school in Vancouver, but hardly knew each other. After school Vallance moved to New York and made trance and progressive house, with releases on Ultra Records and remixes for Sia. Howie spent a year at the Berklee College of Music in Boston, also came to New York and played in a rock band. They found each other again in the car park of a hardware store and began making music together in Howie's apartment, with rock from Howie's past and trance from Vallance's.

The name Bob Moses was suggested by Francis Harris of the label Scissor and Thread, after the New York city planner Robert Moses. Their first EP Hands to Hold appeared in October 2012, followed by Far from the Tree, and in March 2014 they signed with Domino Records. The debut album Days Gone By came out on 18 September 2015, with Tearing Me Up as its best-known song. A remix of it by RAC won a Grammy Award for best remixed recording. Later came Battle Lines in 2018, Desire in 2020, The Silence in Between in 2022 and BLINK in 2025.

Bob Moses shows how house and rock can go together: electronic beats with a singer who has a real songwriter's voice. In this way they stand between the dance floor and the radio, and with Tearing Me Up they also reached the alternative radio chart in the United States.
artiest/bob-moses.listen: Listen to Tearing Me Up from Days Gone By (2015) and notice the beat under the vocals. Notice how the electronic accompaniment and the voice of a rock singer complement each other.

artiest/bob-rock.text:
Bob Rock is a Canadian producer, sound engineer and musician, born in 1954 in Winnipeg. At twelve he moved to Victoria, on Canada's west coast. As a teenager he was a fan of British blues rock bands such as The Yardbirds, Cream and Led Zeppelin. At secondary school he met the singer Paul Hyde, with whom he later founded the band Payola$. Their album No Stranger to Danger (1982) won four Juno Awards, the Canadian music prizes.

In 1976 Rock began as a trainee engineer at the Little Mountain Sound Studios in Vancouver. There he worked with the producer Bruce Fairbairn on albums such as Slippery When Wet by Bon Jovi (1986) and Permanent Vacation by Aerosmith (1987). He then moved over to producing. He made Sonic Temple by The Cult and Dr. Feelgood by Mötley Crüe, both from 1989. His best-known work became Metallica's self-titled album of 1991, the Black Album. For each of those bands it became their best-selling record.

Rock was known for a big, powerful and tightly produced rock sound, with heavy guitars and drums that nevertheless sounded radio-friendly. With Metallica he brought thrash metal to a much larger audience. Later he also produced pop artists such as Michael Bublé, for which he won a Grammy. Bob Rock shows how a producer can define the sound of a whole period in hard rock.
artiest/bob-rock.listen: Listen to Enter Sandman by Metallica. Notice how the song begins quietly with a guitar motif and then grows heavier layer by layer, into a full, tight and mighty guitar sound that is typical of Bob Rock's production.

artiest/bob-thiele.text:
Bob Thiele was an American record producer who worked on many classic jazz albums and labels. He was born on 27 July 1922 in Brooklyn, New York. At fourteen he was already presenting a jazz programme on the radio, and he played clarinet and led a band. At seventeen he founded the label Signature, on which he recorded Lester Young, Erroll Garner and, in 1943, Coleman Hawkins, among others. In 1952 he went to American Decca, where he ran the subsidiary label Coral. There he produced the singer Teresa Brewer, whom he later married, and Buddy Holly at his sessions in New York.

From 1961 to 1969 he ran the label Impulse!. His best-known work there was with John Coltrane, but he also recorded Charles Mingus, Duke Ellington, Sonny Rollins, Archie Shepp and Albert Ayler. His biggest hit as a writer was What a Wonderful World, together with George David Weiss, sung by Louis Armstrong. For it he used the pseudonyms George Douglas and Stanley Clayton, made up from the names of his uncles. At the label BluesWay he produced B. B. King, including the 1967 album Lucille, and John Lee Hooker and T-Bone Walker. In 1968 he founded Flying Dutchman Productions, and the labels Doctor Jazz and Red Baron followed later. In 1995 his memoir appeared, What a Wonderful World. He died on 30 January 1996.

Thiele shows what a producer could do in jazz: give room to adventurous musicians and at the same time bring a melody like What a Wonderful World to a large audience.
artiest/bob-thiele.listen: Listen to What a Wonderful World in the version by Louis Armstrong and notice the soft string accompaniment around his raw voice. Notice how calmly and simply the song is constructed.

artiest/bob-whitlock.text:
Bob Whitlock was an American jazz double bassist, born on 21 January 1931 in Roosevelt, Utah, and died on 20 June 2015 in Long Beach, California. He began playing bass as a teenager and from the early 1950s was active as a studio musician in Los Angeles. There he worked with Gerry Mulligan, Art Pepper, Chet Baker, Stan Getz, Buddy DeFranco, Joe Albany, Jack Sheldon and Warne Marsh. That was the world of West Coast Jazz, in which light, melodic small groups set the tone.

In the second half of the 1950s he also led a small group of his own and attended classes at the University of California. In the early 1960s he worked in France, with Zoot Sims, Vi Redd, Curtis Amy and Victor Feldman. Later in that decade he played with Joe Pass and a great deal with George Shearing. In the 1970s he again worked with Joe Albany.

Whitlock is an example of a bassist who seldom sought the foreground but could be heard everywhere. His name appears on recordings by great names, because bandleaders could count on his playing. Anyone who wants to understand West Coast Jazz hears in such musicians the foundation on which the soloists stood.
artiest/bob-whitlock.listen: Listen to a recording by the Gerry Mulligan Quartet from the 1950s and focus on the double bass. Notice how it marks the beat and the chords, without a piano being there.

artiest/bob-wills.text:
Bob Wills was an American musician, songwriter and bandleader, born on 6 March 1905 on a cotton farm in Kosse, Texas. His father was a fiddle-playing champion and the whole family was musical. There were country parties at home and also ranch dances in West Texas, and so Bob learned fiddle and mandolin at a young age. He is regarded as the founder of western swing and was nicknamed the King of Western Swing. Characteristic were his ah-haa shouts in the music.

After various bands and radio work in the South and West he founded the Texas Playboys in 1934, with himself on fiddle and Tommy Duncan on piano and vocals. In 1937 the guitarist Eldon Shamblin joined, bringing jazz influences and arrangements. The band often played on the radio station KVOO in Tulsa and added, among others, the steel guitarist Leon McAuliffe, the drummer Smokey Dacus and a horn section. Wills liked arrangements with a jazz colour, and the group became nationally popular into the 1940s with Steel Guitar Rag, San Antonio Rose, Stars and Stripes on Iwo Jima and New Spanish Two Step. In 1950 he had two hits in the top ten, Ida Red Likes the Boogie and Faded Love.

In the 1950s he suffered from poor health and money worries, and in 1962 and 1963 he had heart attacks, as a result of which he disbanded the Texas Playboys. In 1968 the Country Music Hall of Fame inducted him, and in 1973 he made an album with his admirer Merle Haggard. He died in 1975. Wills showed that country, jazz and swing could come together in one band.
artiest/bob-wills.listen: Listen to Steel Guitar Rag and notice the steel guitar playing the melody up front. Hear how the rest of the band swings around it, almost like a jazz orchestra.

artiest/bob-wills-and-his-texas-playboys.text:
Bob Wills and His Texas Playboys was the band of Bob Wills, the man regarded as the founder of western swing. Wills founded the group in 1934, after periods with various bands and radio stations in the South and West. The first line-up consisted of Wills on fiddle, Tommy Duncan on piano and vocals, the rhythm guitarist June Whalin, the tenor banjo player Johnnie Lee Wills and Kermit Whalin on steel guitar and bass. The band played regularly on the radio station KVOO in Tulsa, Oklahoma.

In 1937 the guitarist Eldon Shamblin joined, bringing jazz influences and arrangements. Later came Leon McAuliffe on steel guitar, the pianist Al Stricklin, the drummer Smokey Dacus and a horn section, which made the group sound bigger and fuller. Wills liked arrangements with a jazz colour, and the Texas Playboys became nationally known into the 1940s with Steel Guitar Rag, San Antonio Rose, Stars and Stripes on Iwo Jima and New Spanish Two Step. They recorded for Vocalion, Okeh, Columbia and MGM. In 1950 two songs were in the top ten: Ida Red Likes the Boogie and Faded Love. A recording from the 1950s appeared on the soundtrack of The Last Picture Show in 1971, and in 1974 the album For the Last Time followed.

After two heart attacks in 1962 and 1963 Wills had to disband the band, although he continued to perform solo. He was inducted into the Country Music Hall of Fame in 1968, and in 1999 Wills and the Texas Playboys were given a place in the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame. The band showed that a country band with steel guitar, fiddle and horns could swing like a jazz orchestra.
artiest/bob-wills-and-his-texas-playboys.listen: Listen to San Antonio Rose and notice the interplay of fiddle, steel guitar and horns. Notice how a country band sounds when the arrangements come from swing.

artiest/boban-markovic.text: Boban Marković, from Vladičin Han in southern Serbia, turned his Roma brass band into one of the most famous in the Balkans. At the trumpet festival in Guča he won the prize for best trumpeter five times between 1988 and 2001. His orchestra played in the music for Emir Kusturica's film Underground (1995). Since 2002 his son Marko has played with him, later becoming the most important soloist and arranger.
artiest/boban-markovic.listen: Listen to Wedding Cocec: the tubas stamp out an irregular dance rhythm, and the trumpets play fast, ornamented melodies over it.

artiest/boban-markovic-orkestar.text:
Boban Marković is a Serbian trumpeter and leader of a brass orchestra from Vladičin Han, in southern Serbia. He has a Romani background. The orchestra plays Balkan brass and won the most important prizes at the trumpet festival in Guča, the Dragačevski Sabor, which has been held every August in central Serbia since 1961. In 2000 it won the prize for best orchestra, and Marković himself was named first trumpeter five times between 1988 and 2001.

The albums begin with Čik, čik in 1991 and run through, among others, Hani Rumba, Zlatna Truba and Srce Cigansko to Boban i Marko in 2003, the year of Mundo čoček, and later Go Marko Go!, Balkan Brass Battle and Gipsy Manifesto in 2013. His son Marko has played with him since 2002 and as a seventeen-year-old became the most important soloist and arranger. The orchestra made music for a film by Emir Kusturica, Underground, and played at festivals in dozens of countries, and at many weddings.

The classic brass sound is supplemented by two percussionists and sometimes a young violinist. The music is fast, danceable and full of virtuoso trumpet solos. The orchestra also collaborated with the Austrian group Attwenger and with Frank London.
artiest/boban-markovic-orkestar.listen: Listen to Mundo čoček. Notice how the brass and the percussion lay down a dancing rhythm and how the trumpet plays over it with fast ornaments.

artiest/bobby-brown.text:
Bobby Brown was born in 1969 in Boston and grew up in the Orchard Park Projects in Roxbury, one of eight children. At three he saw his idol James Brown perform, and that awakened his dream of becoming a singer. He sang in a church choir. In 1980, at the age of twelve, he founded the group New Edition together with Michael Bivins and Ricky Bell, at first under the name The Bricks. With hits such as Candy Girl and Cool It Now it grew into a well-known R&B and pop group. In 1985 he left the group for a solo career.

His debut album King of Stage from 1986 contained the R&B number 1 Girlfriend. With Don't Be Cruel in 1988 he broke through: five singles reached the top ten of the American Hot 100, including the number 1 My Prerogative and the award-winning Every Little Step. In 1989 he contributed two songs to the soundtrack of Ghostbusters II. The album Bobby followed in 1992, with Humpin' Around. That same year he married Whitney Houston; their marriage received a great deal of media attention and ended in divorce in 2007.

Brown is regarded, together with his regular partner Teddy Riley, as a pioneer of new jack swing, a mixture of hip hop and R&B. That means hard, tight drum machine rhythms beneath soulful singing with rap running through it. My Prerogative shows how that style sounded in 1988: tough, danceable and direct.
artiest/bobby-brown.listen: Listen to My Prerogative. Notice the hard, mechanical beat and how Brown half raps and half sings, while the lyrics are mainly about his own freedom.

artiest/bobby-byrd.text:
Bobby Byrd was an American soul and funk singer, pianist and songwriter from Toccoa, Georgia. He grew up in the church and from 1952 sang in the gospel group the Gospel Starlighters. At a baseball game in a juvenile detention centre he met the young James Brown. Byrd saw to it that his family supervised Brown's parole, and so began a partnership that would last until 1973.

Byrd's group was by now called the Flames, and Brown first became the drummer and then the lead singer. As the Famous Flames they signed in 1956 with Federal, a subsidiary label of King Records. Their first record was Please, Please, Please. Between 1959 and 1964 hits followed such as Try Me, Think and Lost Someone, and the group appeared on the live album Live at the Apollo from 1963. On the records Brown's name stood out more and more, while Byrd and the others sang the backing vocals and responses.

In 1970 Byrd brought in the young Bootsy Collins, his brother Catfish and their band when Brown's regular musicians had walked out. With that new band Brown immediately recorded Get Up (I Feel Like Being a) Sex Machine. Byrd also made solo work, such as We Are in Love from 1965. His role was that of the steady partner next to the star: he discovered Brown, held the group together and helped lay the foundations of soul and funk. In 2012 he was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame with the Famous Flames. He died in 2007.
artiest/bobby-byrd.listen: Listen to Get Up (I Feel Like Being a) Sex Machine by James Brown. Notice the question-and-answer play: Brown calls out, Byrd answers each time with a short line, while the band keeps rolling beneath them.

artiest/bobby-orlando.text:
Bobby Orlando, also known as Bobby O, is an American producer, songwriter, musician and owner of an independent label, born on 10 January 1958. He is the son of a teacher from a suburb of New York and turned down a scholarship for classical music because he would rather make glam rock. In the late 1970s he turned to disco and shortly afterwards started his own label, O Records. He is regarded as one of the founders of Hi-NRG, a fast dance music with synthesizers.

His productions are recognisable by dense synthesizers, rolling bass lines and loud percussion, with a powerful beat and vocals in new wave style. He played many instruments himself, from keyboards and guitar to trumpet and saxophone. The sound of little bells and robotic sequencers can be heard in She Has a Way, The Best Part of Breakin' Up and Native Love (Step by Step). As a solo artist he had hits such as She Has a Way and How to Pick Up Girls. With the project The Flirts, with constantly changing female singers, came Passion, Danger and Helpless. With the film star Divine he made club anthems such as Native Love (Step by Step) and Love Reaction. He also produced The Fast, later Man 2 Man.

In 1983 Neil Tennant sought him out in New York. Tennant and Chris Lowe admired his sound, and they later called Passion by The Flirts the most important song of their lives. Orlando produced the first two singles of the Pet Shop Boys, including the original version of West End Girls from 1984, and recorded twelve songs with them, including the first versions of It's a Sin and I Get Excited. In this way his influence reaches far beyond his own hits.
artiest/bobby-orlando.listen: Listen to Passion by The Flirts and notice the beat, the little bells and the synthesizer bass. Try to hear why the Pet Shop Boys so admired this sound.

artiest/bobby-timmons.text:
Bobby Timmons was an American jazz pianist and composer, born on 19 December 1935 in Philadelphia, the son of a minister. His parents and several uncles and aunts played piano, and he studied with an uncle, Robert Habershaw, who also taught McCoy Tyner. His first performances were in his grandfather's church, which coloured his later playing. He grew up in the same neighbourhood as the Heath brothers and Lee Morgan. In 1954 he moved to New York and played with Kenny Dorham, Chet Baker, Sonny Stitt and Maynard Ferguson, among others.

He became known as a member of Art Blakey's Jazz Messengers, from July 1958 to September 1959 and from February 1960 to June 1961, and in between in the band of Cannonball Adderley. The saxophonist Benny Golson brought him to Blakey and said that he could play both bebop and funky. His compositions from those years had commercial success: Moanin', Dat Dere and This Here. In the early and mid 1960s he led piano trios that toured and recorded a great deal, with albums such as This Here Is Bobby Timmons and Little Barefoot Soul.

Timmons is strongly associated with soul jazz, a style he helped to start, with deceptively simple, bluesy melodies. Drink and drugs held back his career, and he died on 1 March 1974 of cirrhosis of the liver, aged thirty-eight. Critics still consider his contribution to jazz underrated.
artiest/bobby-timmons.listen: Listen to Moanin' by Art Blakey and the Jazz Messengers and notice the question and answer between the piano and the horns. Hear how a church-like, bluesy theme carries the band along.

artiest/bobo-stenson.text:
Bobo Stenson, born Bo Gustav Stenson on 4 August 1944 in Västerås, is a Swedish jazz pianist and composer. From the age of eight he studied for fifteen years with the pianist and professor Werner Wolf Glaser, a Jewish refugee from Cologne. He began with a classical education, but soon chose jazz and as a schoolboy played with Börje Frederiksson and Palle Danielsson. After secondary school he spent some time in Paris and played there at the Blue Note Club. In 1963 he ended up in Stockholm, where he accompanied many visiting Americans, such as Sonny Rollins, Stan Getz and Gary Burton. From the start he also worked closely with Don Cherry, when the latter was living in Scandinavia.

In the 1970s he played in many groups, including Rena Rama with Palle Danielsson, in a trio with Arild Andersen and Jon Christensen and in Oriental Wind with the Turkish percussionist Okay Temiz. Later he played with Jan Garbarek. In 1988 he joined the quartet of Charles Lloyd and from 1996 he appeared at major festivals with the groups of Tomasz Stańko. His records appeared mainly on ECM, from Underwear in 1971 to trio albums such as Goodbye in 2005 and Sphere in 2023.

The Bobo Stenson Trio, with the bassist Anders Jormin and the drummer Jon Fält, has existed for more than fifty years. In 2006 Stenson received the Swedish honour Litteris et Artibus. He belongs to the pianists who gave Scandinavian jazz a distinctive, restrained and lyrical sound.
artiest/bobo-stenson.listen: Listen to a piece from the album Goodbye (2005) and notice the space between the notes. Try to hear how piano, bass and drums talk with one another instead of following one another.

artiest/boef.text:
Boef is the stage name of Sofiane Boussaadia, a Dutch-language rapper and vlogger with French nationality, born on 28 February 1993. He was born near Paris to Algerian parents. At four he lived with an uncle in Eindhoven, later for two years in Houston, Texas, and at thirteen he moved to Alkmaar. The word boef means villain in Dutch. After a period in detention he focused on rap. Through his friend Otie he came to Zonamo Underground, which invited him for a session in February 2015. That session was viewed more than a million times on YouTube within a short time.

After the Zonamo session he signed with Zonamo Underground and within a year became one of the most popular rappers in the Netherlands, after Lil' Kleine and Ronnie Flex. His first EP, Gewoon Boef, came out in February 2016 and reached number four in the Album Top 100. In April 2016 followed the breakthrough hit Lauw, with a video shot in Dubai with the producer Harun B. His first album Slaaptekort appeared in March 2017 and was the album with the most streams on its day of release in the Netherlands, a record previously held by Ed Sheeran's ÷. Later followed Allemaal Een Droom in 2020 and Luxeprobleem in 2023. He also has a vlog channel with videos about his daily life.

Boef belongs to the generation of Dutch rappers who broke through via YouTube and streaming, with a mixture of street stories and melodic, almost sung rap. In 2024 he also started the fast-food chain Chick and Cheez.
artiest/boef.listen: Listen to Lauw from 2016 and notice how he switches between rapping and singing. Hear how the melody and the repetition make the song stick.

artiest/boh-foi-toch.text:
Boh Foi Toch is an Achterhoek band that formed in August 1989. The name means something like 'goodness me, what a thing'. Jan Manschot left Normaal in early 1989 and really no longer wanted to drum. When he was asked whether Hans Keuper could play at a wedding party, the two performed as a duo. They liked it, and Manschot phoned the guitarist Ferdi Joly, who brought along the bassist Willem te Molder. The first official performance was on 1 January 1990 at the Achterhoekgala in the Concordia hall in Hengelo. The band had rehearsed only five songs and therefore played them twice.

The band makes music in the vein of Tex-Mex, Cajun and zydeco. Cajun is the folk music of the originally French inhabitants of Louisiana, while zydeco leans more on a Black tradition. The language used became Low Saxon. Hans Keuper plays the accordion and sings. The albums include Zeet de jongs from 1992, Veur Pauwen En Poeten from 1993, Den Stroatfox En Andern from 1995, Boekspek from 1997 and SÒH! from 2015. In 1997 Han Mali joined on drums, and after Joly left in 2005 Paul Kemper joined on guitar.

The band shows that American folk styles can also feel at home in a Dutch regional language. They celebrated anniversaries in 2015, 2020 and 2025, and in 2021 Keuper won the first Willem Sluiter Prize, which is given to someone who draws positive attention to the Achterhoek.
artiest/boh-foi-toch.listen: Listen to Nen Amerikaan. Notice the accordion, which here brings the sound of Louisiana to the Achterhoek, and the Low Saxon lyrics.

artiest/bomba-estereo.text:
Bomba Estéreo is a Colombian band founded in Bogotá in 2005 by Simón Mejía. Their music is called electro-tropical or psychedelic cumbia. The roots lie in 2001, when Mejía, formerly a member of the Colombian rock band Charconautas, was part of a loose collective of musicians and visual artists under the name A.M. 770. Their influences were Colombian groups such as Sidestepper and Bloque de Búsqueda, who in the late 1990s mixed traditional rhythms such as salsa and cumbia with modern electronic beats. In 2005 the project became mainly his solo work and the name changed to Bomba Estéreo.

The first result was the mini-album Vol. 1. In New York Mejía secured an international distribution deal with Nacional Records. One of the singers on that record was Liliana Li Saumet from Santa Marta, whom he then chose as permanent singer. By the second album, Estalla from 2008, Bomba Estéreo was a real band, with Saumet on vocals, Diego Cadavid on percussion, Julián Salazar on guitar, Kike Egurrola on drums and Mejía on bass and keyboards. In the United States it was released as Blow Up. With the single Fuego the group won new fans outside Colombia, and in 2010 the viewers of MTV Iggy chose it as the best new band in the world. Later followed Elegancia tropical in 2012, Amanecer in 2015, Ayo in 2017 and Deja in 2021.

In 2010 the band recorded Pump Up the Jam by Technotronic for a Levi's advertising campaign, as Ponte Bomb. Bomba Estéreo showed how Caribbean and Colombian rhythms could melt with dance music into a new style, putting Colombia on the world map of the dance floor.
artiest/bomba-estereo.listen: Listen to Fuego from Estalla (2008) and notice the combination of a tropical rhythm and electronic sounds. Hear how the singer half raps and half sings above the beat.

artiest/bon-iver.text:
Bon Iver is an American indie folk band founded in 2006 by the singer-songwriter Justin Vernon in Eau Claire, Wisconsin. It began as a solo project and later became a band with, among others, Sean Carey, Michael Lewis and Jenn Wasner. The name comes from French, bon hiver, good winter, and is taken from a greeting in the TV series Northern Exposure.

After the break-up of his band DeYarmond Edison, the end of a relationship and an illness, Vernon returned to Wisconsin. At the end of 2006 he withdrew for several months to a cabin belonging to his father. There, without a plan, came the album For Emma, Forever Ago, which he released independently in July 2007. He played all the instruments himself and treated the songs with many overdubs. He wrote the lyrics to the sound of syllables in a melody without words.

The second album Bon Iver, Bon Iver won a Grammy for best alternative album in 2012. Then followed 22, a Million in 2016, i,i in 2019, which was nominated for album of the year, and SABLE, fABLE in 2025. The sound is soft and intimate, with a high falsetto voice, acoustic guitar and layered vocals. Bon Iver showed how a bedroom recording made in isolation could grow into a worldwide indie folk classic.
artiest/bon-iver.listen: Listen to Skinny Love. Notice the guitar, the layered vocals and Vernon's raw, breaking voice, which sounds as if he is sitting right next to you.
